newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares held onto swift early morning gains on Tuesday to finish firmly up on the back of a wave of positive sentiment sweeping through the market, dealers said.
In a reverse of trends seen throughout much of 1996 a strong rand has boosted share prices as dealers lick their lips at the prospect of a resultant jump in corporate earnings.
A firm bond market and a healthy outlook for eventual interest rate cuts has also seen positive sentiment rise.
"The market has been quite firm on all fronts, triggered off by the strong rand this morning and that held through all day," one dealer said.
Dealers said the market's strength was an indication that many fund managers -- who hid in cash markets for most of 1996 -- may soon switch more investment into equities.
With 667 million shares changing hands, volumes were healthy and attracted interest from foreign buyers as well as from futures players, dealers said.
The market is expected to continue its rise on Wednesday, though dealers did not expect huge gains.
Earlier in the day the Johannesburg Stock Exchange was hit by technical problems that, while not disrupting trade, did slow the flow of price information.

As deals ticked through after the close of trade the all-share index was indicated up 52.5 points to 6,766.0 as industrials put on 46.6 points to 8,108.2. Some dealers said heavily index-weighted stocks had fared particularly well and may have artificially boosted the day's rise.
Among blue chip gainers were De Beers which finished up 25 cents at 141.75 and Richemont which ended up 25 cents to 63.25 rand.

Golds also had a good day with the index roaring ahead to be indicated up 49.3 points, or 3.68 percent, to 1,388.3. Kloof ended up 190 cents at 34.50 rand and Vaal Reefs added 600 cents to 309.00 rand.

A bullion price that seemed to have firmed above $345 was the main supporting factor. Dealers said the giddy fall of the gold price may now have bottomed out and -- in the short-term at least -- a rally may be just around the corner.
But they cautioned that not too much should be read into such one day rises. "Golds shares were so bombed out anyway that they can't really go down anymore," one dealer said.

The platinum sector fared less well with the market digesting poor results released on Monday from Amplats. The firm's stock ended the day down 55 cents to 26.00 rand and its Rustenberg unit dipped 75 cents to 61.25 rand.

Impala Platinum escaped lightly and ended level at 45.75 rand, but analysts said the poor outlook for precious metals prices would probably eventually hit the firm. "The precious metals prices are obviously going to hit Impala," said Bruce Williamson, analyst at SBC Warburg.
The futures market also had a firm day with some buying of equities. The all-share March contract edged up to 6,210/24 from 6,142 as the industrials contract stood at 7,856/63 from 7,829.
The golds contract, buoyed by the bullion price, was at 961/77 from 943.
